summary: Michigan Conservation Department tower in Chippewa County, staffed in 1954 and 1965. A 2016 blog reprints a 1980s sale account and says a tower still stands at Goetzville.

facts.status_note: A 2016 blog post says a tower still stands at Goetzville, without saying whether it is the tower the neighbor bought. No later source was found.

access.note: A 2016 blog post reprints a 1980s sale account in which the adjacent property owner bought the Goetzville tower. The account is hedged, and the post does not say whether the standing tower is that one or whether the public can visit it.

events.note: Ken Weston of Sterlingville was back on the Goetzville fire tower, per the Evening News (April 21, 1954).
Jim Pudelko hired on as a Class-B towerman and worked about a year as a towerman before military service.

notes_for_editor: The 110 ft height is a former towerman's memory, converted to 33.5 m. The sale to the neighbor and the 'standing' status rest on one 2016 blog post, which reprints a July 2016 Sault News article; the source gives no year for the sale, so no sale event is recorded. The sale account sits in a first-person passage and is hedged, so it is not attributed to the blog author. No later check of the site. A Mapcarta/OpenStreetMap point named 'Goetzville Lookout Tower' sits in Raber Township, which corroborates a tower feature only. The Goetzville Oral History page has no tower mention. No build date found.
